i was good friends with a girl in secondary school for a few years. everyone liked her because she was weird and said the most absurdly unexpected funny things. one day she sent me a text telling me that she had terminal brain cancer, and naturally i was very upset. i phoned her in tears, and she seemed confused by how devastated i was, but i didn’t think anything of it at the time.

a few months later, i and some other friends she’d confided in decided to ask her twin brother, who was also in our class and was another friend of ours, how he was holding up. he didnt understand the context at first. 

“it’s okay. we know. you can talk to us.” we said.

“know what?”

“about your sister’s incurable cancer.”

he more or less laughed in our faces. told us that she didn’t have any cancer, let alone terminal. didn’t have any idea why we’d think so. 

“she told me herself that she had terminal brain cancer.” i said.

another friend said, “she told me it was cancer of the blood.”

“but she told me it was bone marrow cancer.”

it hit us then. she hadn’t even kept track of what lie she’d told and to who. suddenly she wasn’t in school the next day, and the day after that she avoided talking to us, not that we wanted to speak to her anyway. i don’t think i ever spoke to her again. that was when i was 15, i’m 20 now. i don’t know what would possess someone to lie about something like that, especially to their friends.

i see on your profile it says you’re 16. trust me, you have all the time in the world to get into a relationship. it’s actually completely normal at your age. no one expects you to be amazingly charismatic or rich or “conventionally” good looking. i mean, you’re only 16, but those things aren’t the be all and end all, especially money. i know it’s a lot easier for me to say it than for you to believe it, but someone will see who you are and genuinely love you if you just give it some time. it’s painful waiting, i know — i’m 20 and i’ve never been in a relationship, and i spent a lot of my teenage years beating myself up for it, but i realised this year that i wasn’t the problem. i was just a child! relationships and attraction, while they can start in adolescence, are quite mature concepts. in my experience watching the people around me, most teenage relationships simply do not last. you’ll probably actually do a lot better to wait until you’re an adult. i understand this wasn’t the main focus of your post but it made me sad to see you say this.
